id: title:carlos-marchal-ph:reject a variable used inside its own declaration

review.posthog_relevance: Adds bytecode compiler support for distinguishing initialized vs uninitialized local variables, enabling detection of self-referential assignment errors and preventing runtime errors from reading uninitialized locals.
review.reason: Adds a boolean field `initialized` to the `Local` dataclass and updates `_declare_local` to record initialization status. P1.F1.H1 adds the field; P1.F1.H2 updates the declaration and adds a helper `_reject_uninitialized_local` to raise a `QueryError` if a local is not initialized. observations.behavior: Adds a boolean field `initialized` to the `Local` dataclass, defaulting to `True`.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows bytecode compiler to distinguish between a local variable slot that has been declared but not yet assigned a value versus one that has been assigned, which is necessary for detecting self-referential assignment errors.

observations.behavior: Updates `_declare_local` to accept an `initialized` parameter and passes it to the new `Local` instance.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the bytecode compiler to record whether a variable is initialized at the time of its declaration, distinguishing between immediate assignment and deferred assignment.

observations.behavior: Adds a new helper function `_reject_uninitialized_local` that raises a `QueryError` if a local variable is not initialized.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides a check to prevent the bytecode compiler from generating instructions that would read an uninitialized local variable, which could lead to runtime errors or incorrect results.
